62	| --- | --- |
63	| Signature | `provider-dispatch/unknown-id-falls-back` |
64	| First seen | review request and head SHA |
65	| Evidence | affected path, behavior, and reproduction |
66	| Disposition | one of the four standard dispositions |
67	| Resolution | fix reference, issue link, or rejection reason |
68	| Verification | command, test, or inspection result |

77	2. Targeted re-review of the batched fix delta.
78	3. Exceptional targeted pass only when the fix introduced a credible `P0` or `P1`.

86	
87	- a proposed fix adds a new subsystem or architectural layer;
88	- the changed-file set or behavioral surface grows materially beyond the contract;
89	- a finding requires selecting among product or architecture alternatives;
90	- the same root cause returns after an evidenced resolution;
91	- the reviewer requires implementation of explicitly linked deferred work;
92	- review comments outnumber distinct root causes by a large margin;
93	- a pass is clean and another pass is requested without a changed patch.
94

98	
99	A durable follow-up issue should contain:
100	
101	- a duplicate check against open and recently closed issues;
102	- origin PR and relevant review link;
103	- one root cause, not a transcript dump;
104	- current behavior and material impact;
105	- why it is outside the current contract;
106	- acceptance criteria;
107	- known constraints and verification expectations.
108	
109	A local TODO is optional. Use it only at a concrete code seam and link the issue. Do not let a TODO silently become a second specification or a reviewer-enforced blocker.
110	
111	The reviewer should identify a follow-up candidate, not order or perform the external write. The parent development pipeline decides the disposition, checks authority, deduplicates, creates the issue when authorized, and links the result back to the originating thread.
112	
113	Default every admitted P2 and P3 finding to an issue-ready follow-up unless an existing issue already represents the root cause. This default does not authorize issue spam: group symptoms, reject aesthetic-only preferences, and reuse existing issues.

119	- **Scope inflation:** do not require P2 or P3 work in the current PR merely because it is valuable.
120	- **Severity inflation:** do not label maintainability feedback P1 just to force visibility.

6	
7	- `packages/contracts` - Zod schemas and types. Depends on zod only.
8	- `packages/domain` - pure logic over the contracts. No I/O.
9	- `packages/engine` - executor, run manager, node handlers, written against ports. `@graphgoblin/engine/testing` has fakes for every port.
10	- `packages/infrastructure` - Node implementations of the engine ports, one folder per concern (`src/sqlite`, `src/fs`, `src/process`, `src/http`, `src/scheduler`), each with its own `index.ts` and an `@graphgoblin/infrastructure/<folder>` subpath. Folders may import each other.
11	- `packages/adapter-*` - reserved for optional external-service adapters with their own dependency (`adapter-codex`, `adapter-jev`). New packages only at real boundaries: a different runtime, reuse by several apps, or an optional or licence-sensitive dependency (ADR-0014). Otherwise add a folder.
12	- `apps/*` - composition roots: `api`, `mcp`, `web`, `plugin-codex`, `plugin-claude`.
13	- `tooling/` - shared config and the repository gate scripts.
14	
15	Layer rules are enforced by `pnpm check:layers` (declared workspace dependencies) and `pnpm check:deps` (dependency-cruiser). Reach other packages only through their `@graphgoblin/*` entry points.
16	
17	Node 22 LTS is the supported runtime; installation, development and gates need Node 22.22.2 or later, and other majors are unsupported. Select it for the whole shell before running commands. On this Windows host that is the project-scoped runtime, leaving the machine's own Node untouched: `$env:PATH = "$env:USERPROFILE\.claude\codex-runs\GraphGoblin\runtime\node-v22.23.4-win-x64;$env:PATH"` in PowerShell, or `export PATH="$HOME/.claude/codex-runs/GraphGoblin/runtime/node-v22.23.4-win-x64:$PATH"` in Git Bash. Confirm `node --version` reports `v22.22.2` or later. `.nvmrc`, CI and the container use major 22 (CI and the container take the latest 22.x); root `engines.node` and `devEngines.runtime` declare `^22.22.2`, with `onFail: error` refusing every pnpm command on an older Node 22 or another major. pnpm runs package scripts with the first `node` on PATH. Run gates through pnpm: calling `node_modules/.bin/turbo` directly bypasses this check, and Turbo's cache key ignores the running Node version. See ADR-0040 and ADR-0058.
18	
19	## Rules
20	
21	- `tooling` participates in the shared Vitest V8 coverage gate and the Turbo lint pipeline; its independent built-app acceptance suites remain separate.
22	- Every package must keep unit-test coverage at or above 90% of lines and branches. `pnpm test:coverage` fails otherwise. Do not lower thresholds or add exclusions beyond generated code.
23	- `pnpm typecheck` runs `tsc -b tsconfig.build.json && tsc -p tsconfig.json` in every TypeScript package (the web app runs `tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit`), so test files and fixtures are type-checked too; fix their types rather than casting to `any`. `tooling` is JavaScript: it has lint and coverage, not a typecheck task.
24	- Tests, lint, and typechecking need no prior build in the TypeScript packages: each lists a `development` export condition pointing at its TypeScript source, which TypeScript, Vitest, and ESLint resolve. Node at runtime loads `dist/`, so run `pnpm build` before starting an app. A new TypeScript workspace package must follow the same export-map shape. `tooling` tests drive the built API and web app: Turbo builds them first, and a direct package test needs `pnpm build` first.
25	- API subprocess tests build the API first through Turbo's `test` and `test:coverage` task dependencies.
26	- Only permissive licences (MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD, ISC). `pnpm check:licenses` enforces the allowlist in `tooling/license-allowlist.json`; add a line to `docs/research/licenses.md` for every new dependency.
27	- Relative imports use explicit `.js` extensions (NodeNext). Zod 4: use `.prefault({})` for object defaults whose fields have defaults.
28	- Keep docs in sync: a behaviour change updates the relevant numbered doc; a decision change adds an ADR.
29	- Clean design over backward compatibility, until the owner says otherwise (2026-10-04): the product is not released and has no production users. Do not build compatibility schemas, deprecated input paths, tolerant parsing of old data shapes, or dual code paths. Change the contract to its clean shape. A schema change within the current format is an ordinary Drizzle migration that keeps existing data; Drizzle migrations are for schema changes only. Stored content that a change makes invalid is never rewritten by migration code: the CHANGELOG upgrade note says which stored values to correct and how (for example the SQL), and the orchestrator corrects the owner's store by hand (ADR-0062). A change of the stored, export or device-draft format moves the current format and refuses older data clearly, with no converter, and the owner resets with `--reset` (ADR-0042); say so, and what exports or clients must change, in the CHANGELOG upgrade notes.
30	- Before picking up a GitHub issue, read `docs/15-issue-workflow.md` for its gate, routing, and delivery rules.
31	- Commits carry no assistant attribution of any kind.
32	
33	## Commands
34	
35	On Windows PowerShell, call `pnpm.cmd` (the default execution policy blocks `pnpm.ps1`); Git Bash and cmd can use `pnpm` directly.
36	
37	```
38	pnpm install
39	pnpm build
40	pnpm test:coverage
41	pnpm lint
42	pnpm docs:generate  # regenerate docs/reference after a node schema or route change
43	pnpm check          # typecheck, lint, layers, deps, coverage, licences, generated docs
44	```

# Changelog

All notable changes to GraphGoblin. The design is in [docs/](docs/README.md); the user guide is [docs/guide/](docs/guide/README.md).

## Unreleased

- Codex structured calls create short scratch names with exclusive `mkdir`, retrying at most
  four `EEXIST` collisions and preserving every colliding directory (#363). This avoids the
  Windows `mkdtemp` failure under the tested 226-character temp root; OS/CLI path limits remain.
  Request/configured working directories and cancellation/error cleanup precedence are unchanged.

- Windows launcher identity and ownership checks own their descendants in private Windows jobs
  (#459), drain both output streams within a bounded work window and collect failed checks
  before displaying errors. Initial checks retain the 15-second work cap, with up to two seconds
  for cleanup; held-store retries reserve that cleanup time and retain the last held guidance
  when a conclusive new sample cannot fit. Raw helper output is never displayed or logged.
  Ownership output is parsed once as strict JSON before whitespace normalization; duplicate
  decoded keys, unknown fields and JavaScript-only syntax refuse startup. Cleanup is confirmed
  only when the complete process/job/stream observation finishes before the two-second deadline;
  a later completion keeps the unconfirmed-cleanup outcome (D166).
  Caller admission now carries one absolute work cutoff through helper preparation, creation,
  validation and result consumption. Setup cannot restart the held retry's clock or admit a
  free sample inside its reserved cleanup interval; equality at the cutoff refuses (D167).
  **Upgrade:** rebuild and reinstall the launcher. Windows 10 or Windows Server 2016 or later
  with compatible nested jobs is required, including for warm shortcut clicks. A restricted host
  can refuse the shortcut while an existing gateway remains callable at its current address.
  No store, lock or export format change and no reset. PR #460 remains separately held.

- API startup now prints one stack-free line for held or unverifiable data-directory,

A UI change does not qualify merely because it changes a screen; a missing or failing test, or a known defect, is engineering work, not a reason for the label. # Review 1 of 3: #363 short exclusive scratch allocation (Claude opposite-family, read-only)

**Decision: CHANGES_REQUIRED.** The runtime change is correct and I'm not asking for any code change. The blocker is that the docs and CHANGELOG added by this patch say the 226-character temp root is supported. In the production Codex path, structured calls under that root very likely still fail. The fix is a short wording correction in two files.

## Binding
- **Head:** `76beeb0f2e99343697578c2713ac06f80d59e7b5`. I confirmed this by reading the branch ref `refs/heads/codex/gg-i4-363-structured`.
- **Tree / parent:** `2544bc2913f9cec0d95a215ea631ab62c7985c1d` / `02351e2fb932b3be44e7cc3fb3943a61d568226c`. Both come from `source-binding.json`; I couldn't check them myself.
- **Checkout vs patch:** I read `structured.ts` and `structured.test.ts` in full, plus the docs/06 and CHANGELOG hunks in place. They match the `author.patch` post-image.
- **Unchanged method:** `complete()` is byte-identical to the baseline file in `baseline-structured.original.ts`.

## Findings

### F1 (P2, in scope, blocking): the docs claim the 226-character root works, but the real Codex path still fails there
Signature: `structured-long-temp/sdk-output-schema-mkdtemp`

**Root cause.** Every structured call sends an output schema to the Codex SDK:
- `structured.ts:76` always sets `outputSchema`, and `harness.ts:249` passes it on.
- The production harness uses the real SDK client (`adapters.ts:17`, `harness.ts:104-115`, `client.ts:48`).
- In `@openai/codex-sdk` 0.160.0, the turn calls `createOutputSchemaFile` (`dist/index.js:55`). That calls `fs.mkdtemp(path.join(os.tmpdir(), "codex-output-schema-"))` (`dist/index.js:13`), with no fallback.
- No code in `apps` or `packages` changes the process temp root, so this directory goes under the same root as the scratch directory.

**The arithmetic.** At a 226-character root, the SDK's template is 226 + 1 + 20 + 6 = **253 characters**. The repo's own measurement says Windows `mkdtemp` fails with `ENAMETOOLONG` from 248 to 258 characters (`docs/qa/2026-10-19-wp-f5-launch-diagnosis.md:108`). The author's own baseline also shows Node 22.23.4 `mkdtemp` failing at 256 on this host.

**Impact.**
- **Production callers:** the engine's decision and coerce-repair calls pass no working directory (`docs/06:606-608`), so they use exactly this path.
- **What changes:** the failure still happens; it just moves later. After the patch, the scratch directory is created and a `codex mcp list` check runs (`client.ts:45`, no paid turn). The SDK's `mkdtemp` then fails, and the error comes back through the harness's generic error classification instead of the allocator's raw error.
- **Why the existing hedges don't cover it:** they mention paths created *inside* the scratch directory and "arbitrary" CLI operations. The SDK directory sits next to the scratch directory, is created on every call, and fails for the same `mkdtemp` reason the patch says it avoids.
- **Wording that is wrong:** `docs/06:601` says "This supports the tested 226-character temporary root". `CHANGELOG.md:9` says "This avoids the Windows `mkdtemp` failure under the tested 226-character temp root". That breaks AGENTS.md "Keep docs in sync" and the brief's rules: no general long-path claim, and docs bounded to the real case.
- **Delivery risk:** #363 / U4.4 could be closed on a claim the production path contradicts.
- **Why the tests missed it:** they use `FakeHarness`, which never reaches the SDK.

**Required in this PR (docs only, no runtime change):**
- `docs/06:601-602` and `CHANGELOG.md:9` should say only that the adapter's own scratch directory no longer fails at the tested root.
- Both should say that real Codex structured turns at that root are still limited by the SDK creating its output-schema directory with `mkdtemp` under the same temp root, and link a follow-up.
- The handoff report should say the same.

**This finding can be refuted without a paid turn.** An existing test setup runs the real SDK against a fake CLI (`isolation.test.ts:84-99`); the test at `:287-308` already sends a `CodexStructured` call through it and checks `--output-schema`.
